bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Capital Market Fluctuations Risk — The Company's portfolio of equities, bonds, and financial assets is inherently linked to domestic and global capital markets, making its revenue and asset values sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, interest rate movements, investor sentiment, and geopolitical events.
- Geopolitical and Macroeconomic Risk — Escalation of geopolitical tensions, particularly the USâIran conflict, and elevated crude oil prices pose significant risks to the domestic economy and financial markets, potentially leading to a more cautious and defensive economic environment.
- Regulatory and Compliance Risk — As an RBI-registered NBFC, the Company must adhere to evolving regulatory requirements; non-compliance could impact operations, reputation, and the ability to conduct business.
- Credit Risk and Risk in Investee Companies — The long-term, equity-focused investment strategy exposes the Company to the financial health and performance of investee companies, including those within the Promoter group, where adverse developments could impair investment value.
- Liquidity Risk — The decision to conserve resources and not declare a dividend, along with the need to maintain sufficient funds for investment and working capital, underscores the importance of managing liquidity in a volatile environment.
- Operational and Fraud Risk — With a small team of six employees, the Company faces risks related to operational efficiency, internal controls, and potential fraud, which are managed through the Risk Management Committee and internal audit processes.
- Sustainability and ESG-related Risks — The Risk Management Committee explicitly identifies ESG-related risks as part of the enterprise risk framework, reflecting the growing importance of environmental, social, and governance factors in investment decisions and stakeholder expectations.

business.body: Summit Securities Limited operates as a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) registered with the Reserve Bank of India, classified as a non-deposit-accepting entity. The company's principal business is making investments, with a portfolio predominantly composed of long-term equity holdings and investments in companies where it is part of the promoter group. Revenue is substantially derived from these investments, including dividend income, and the value of its financial assets is inherently linked to domestic and global capital market conditions.

outlook.body:
- Preserve capital and manage risk prudently in volatile financial markets.
- Identify attractive investment opportunities and generate sustainable risk-adjusted returns.
- Maintain a long-term investment orientation, predominantly in equity markets and promoter-group companies.
- Embed Enterprise Risk Management within the business culture through a structured, disciplined risk strategy.
- Dividend proposed by the Board is subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, except for interim dividends. No explicit dividend policy, buyback, debt reduction, or reinvestment philosophy stated beyond this standard provision.
- The Company has an anti-corruption/anti-bribery policy, approved by the Board and published on its website, as part of its governance framework under Principle 1 of the NGRBC.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company, a Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) registered with the Reserve Bank of India as a Non-Deposit Accepting NBFC, derives a substantial portion of its revenue from investments. Its investments are typically long-term in nature and predominantly in the equity markets, including companies where it is part of the Promoter group. All investment decisions are reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board of Directors periodically. The Company has one wholly owned subsidiary, Instant Holdings Limited. There are no material changes and commitments affecting the financial position of the Company which have occurred between the end of the financial year on March 31, 2026, and the date of this report. The Company has neither given any loans or advances nor guarantees during the year under review.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue substantially derived from investments; portfolio value inherently linked to domestic and global capital markets, influenced by macroeconomic conditions, interest rates, investor sentiment, and geopolitical events.
- Global economy grew 3.3% in CY2025; OECD projects ~2.9% for CY2026 and 3.0% for CY2027, contingent on no further escalation of geopolitical tensions including the US–Iran conflict.
- India's real GDP growth estimated at ~7.6% in FY2025-26; RBI projects 6.9% growth and 4.6% inflation for FY2026-27, factoring in heightened geopolitical tensions, elevated crude oil prices, and potential supply chain disruptions.
- Operating environment for financial markets expected to remain volatile; the Company's ability to generate sustainable risk-adjusted returns will be critical to long-term success.
- Net profit increased mainly on account of higher dividend income, resulting in an increase in Return on Net Worth.

The Company's ability to preserve capital, manage risk prudently, identify attractive investment opportunities and generate sustainable risk-adjusted returns will continue to be critical to its long-term success.

The Risk Management Committee has formulated a Risk Management Policy to embed Enterprise Risk Management within the business culture, ensuring a structured, disciplined, and consistent risk strategy.

Escalation of the Middle East conflict and its impact on crude oil prices pose significant risks to the domestic economy and the Company's investment portfolio, with the operating environment expected to remain volatile.

sk.overview: India's digital financial services and NBFC-led retail lending sector serves a large, young, credit-underpenetrated mass market. Formalization (GST, JAM/India Stack, eKYC), rising smartphone/internet penetration and low data costs are enabling tech-led NBFCs and fintechs to underwrite and serve borrowers that conventional banks have historically underserved, particularly in unsecured personal loans and loan-against-property.
